source.title: Cultivating Competence, Self-Efficacy, and Intrinsic Interest Through Proximal Self-Motivation
source.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 41(3):586-598

confidence_rationale: Classic controlled experiment isolating goal GRANULARITY: identical material, only the goal framing varied (proximal subgoals vs single distal goal vs no goals). Proximal subgoals produced the strongest gains on every measure; distal goals 'had no demonstrable effects'. Directly supports Strand G (proximal subgoals sustain distal motivation) and the maintenance thesis (a bare superordinate goal does not by itself drive sustained effort -- it must be decomposed). Confidence 0.60: small-N developmental study (40 children, ~10/cell), single domain, and the mechanism ('self-efficacy') has no clean computational analog.
failure_signatures: Distal goal alone was statistically indistinguishable from no goals -- a cautionary datum for any REE design that expects a bare superordinate goal representation to sustain long-horizon effort without intermediate structure.

The mechanism is human self-efficacy self-appraisal; the study conflates subgoals-as-frequent-success-signals with subgoals-as-capability-information, which a computational model would need to separate.
Small N (~10/cell), single domain (arithmetic), four sessions -- noisy effect-size estimates.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Decomposing a distal goal into attainable proximal subgoals produced rapid self-directed learning, mastery, persistence, and intrinsic interest; a matched distal goal alone produced no demonstrable effect over no-goal controls.
mapping.ree_translation: Empirical anchor for cross-level credit: subgoal attainment sustains motivation toward (and commitment to) the superordinate goal, where the bare distal goal does not. Grounds a candidate `cross_level_subgoal_credit` extending MECH-217's along-trajectory propagation to UP-the-hierarchy propagation (subgoal success -> reinforced parent-goal commitment), and supports INV-034's premise that goal maintenance is an achievement requiring structure, not a default.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human developmental behaviour mediated by self-efficacy self-appraisal -- no direct computational analog. The result motivates the cross-level-credit mechanism but does not isolate it (between-condition contrasts, not a manipulated internal credit signal). Effect magnitudes are from a small single-domain sample.
mapping.source_context: Children 7-10y with arithmetic deficits; 4-session self-directed learning, between-subjects goal-framing manipulation.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical and cleanly designed but small-N developmental; the distal-goal null is the most transferable datum. Goal-gradient anchors (Hull 1932; Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006, JMR 43(1):39-58, doi 10.1509/jmkr.43.1.39) corroborate the proximity->effort gradient.
